writeup.headline: Oracle rates Hold: strong cloud-driven growth offset by negative cash flow, heavy debt and a collapsing share price.
writeup.thesis: Oracle scores 45, right at the bottom edge of Hold, as fast growth pulls against weak cash flow, balance sheet and price trend. Growth scores 86, with TTM revenue growth of 21.6% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 29.6% year on year, and growth sped up by 9.0 pp from the previous quarter. Quality is middling at 48: the operating margin is 32.1%, but the FCF margin excluding prepayments is -60.3% as AI data-centre spending runs ahead of revenue, and the diluted share count is up 3.1% year on year. The balance sheet scores just 13, with cash covering only 0.3 times debt and free cash flow negative. Valuation scores 41: in absolute terms P/S of 5.5x and EV/EBIT of 20.9x are moderate, and the stock is cheap against its own history (P/FCF not comparable). The trend score of 3 reflects a price 53.6% below its 52-week high.
key_risks: Free cash flow is deeply negative, and management only guides to positive FCF in 2H FY28, so funding depends on debt and customer prepayments.
Weak balance sheet: cash to debt of 0.3 with net debt rising against negative FCF.
Customer concentration: Cantor estimates OpenAI accounts for about half of Oracle's RPO.
Litigation, including the Oracle Health breach affecting about 19.9 million people, an ongoing securities class action and a new employee RSU lawsuit.
Price momentum is very poor: shares down 52.7% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago and 29.9 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days.
what_would_change: A drop of just 1 point in the composite score would move the rating to Sell, for example from further price weakness, slowing growth or new negative news.
Reaching Buy needs 20 more points, most plausibly from a recovery in the trend score and improving free cash flow that would lift quality, balance sheet and valuation scores.
Evidence of progress toward positive free cash flow, or confirmation that OpenAI exposure is smaller than estimated, would support an upgrade.
A guidance cut against the reaffirmed FY27 target of at least $90B revenue and $8.10 non-GAAP EPS would push the rating down.
